import React, { useState } from 'react'; import { useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom'; import { motion } from 'framer-motion'; import { FaArrowLeft, FaLandmark, FaBook, FaUsers, FaHistory } from 'react-icons/fa'; import './TribalHeritage.css'; // Six Tribes data with heritage and history const tribes = [ { id: 1, name: 'Toda', image: 'https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1533105079780-92b9be482077?w=600', population: '~1,500', language: 'Toda (Dravidian)', occupation: 'Buffalo herding, dairy work', heritage: 'Famous for distinctive barrel-vaulted huts called "mands", intricate embroidery (pukhoor), and buffalo-centric culture. Their art features geometric patterns in red and black on white cloth.', history: 'The Todas are considered the original inhabitants of the Nilgiri Hills, dating back thousands of years. They have a unique polyandrous marriage system and are one of the most photographed tribes in India. Their culture revolves around the sacred buffalo, and they maintain complex ritual relationships with other Nilgiri tribes.', religion: 'Buffalo worship, animistic beliefs', location: 'Nilgiri plateau, mainly Ooty and surrounding areas' }, { id: 2, name: 'Kota', image: 'https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1544377142212-928c9e80b4ab?w=600', population: '~2,000', language: 'Kota (Dravidian)', occupation: 'Artisans, musicians, blacksmiths', heritage: 'Master craftsmen known for metalwork, pottery, and wood carving. They are traditional musicians who perform at Toda and Badaga ceremonies. Their villages are called "kokars".', history: 'According to legend, the deity Kambattarayan created the Kotas for artisan work. They have a symbiotic relationship with other tribes, providing tools, pottery, and music in exchange for dairy products from Todas and grains from Badagas. Their annual Kol Vaishnavam festival is famous.', religion: 'Hindu with tribal deities, ancestor worship', location: 'Kotagiri and surrounding Nilgiri villages' }, { id: 3, name: 'Kurumba', image: 'https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1588668214407-6ea9e6d8c278?w=600', population: '~10,000', language: 'Kurumba (Dravidian)', occupation: 'Honey collection, forest produce, agriculture', heritage: 'Known as skilled honey hunters and forest dwellers. They have extensive knowledge of medicinal plants and maintain ancient traditions of sustainable forest living. Their art includes basket weaving and tribal paintings.', history: 'The Kurumbas are believed to be among the earliest settlers of the Nilgiris. They traditionally collected honey from cliffs and forests, trading with other tribes. They live in small hamlets on hill slopes and maintain deep spiritual connections to the forest.', religion: 'Animistic, nature worship', location: 'Hill slopes and forest areas across Nilgiris' }, { id: 4, name: 'Irula', image: 'https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1590422749830-5c5e1e1e9a6e?w=600', population: '~5,000', language: 'Irula (Dravidian)', occupation: 'Snake catching, honey gathering, labor', heritage: 'Famous as traditional snake catchers with extraordinary knowledge of reptiles. They practice unique rituals related to snake worship and have extensive knowledge of forest ecology.', history: 'The Irulas migrated to the Nilgiris from the plains of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. They traditionally lived in forest hamlets and were known for catching snakes and gathering forest products. Many now work in plantations while maintaining their cultural identity.', religion: 'Hindu with strong animistic elements, snake worship', location: 'Lower regions and forest fringes of Nilgiris' }, { id: 5, name: 'Paniya', image: 'https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1516426122078-c23e76319801?w=600', population: '~8,000', language: 'Paniya (Dravidian)', occupation: 'Agriculture, plantation labor', heritage: 'Traditional agricultural workers with rich oral traditions. They have distinctive jewelry, tattoos, and folk songs. Their culture emphasizes community living and seasonal festivals.', history: 'The Paniyas are classified as a Primitive Tribal Group. They traditionally practiced shifting cultivation and lived in autonomous settlements. Many now work on tea and coffee plantations while preserving their language and customs.', religion: 'Hindu with tribal deities, ancestor worship', location: 'Throughout Nilgiri district, especially plantation areas' }, { id: 6, name: 'Badaga', image: 'https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1506905925346-21bda4d32df4?w=600', population: '~200,000', language: 'Badaga (Dravidian)', occupation: 'Agriculture, business, education', heritage: 'The largest tribal community in Nilgiris, known for their agricultural prowess and emphasis on education. They maintain elaborate funeral ceremonies (karsh) and have a rich oral literature tradition.', history: 'The Badagas migrated from the Mysore plains of Karnataka around the 16th century after the fall of the Vijayanagar Empire. Despite being migrants, they became the dominant agricultural community and political leaders in the Nilgiris. They maintain complex exchange relationships with Todas, Kotas, and Kurumbas.', religion: 'Hindu (Shaiva sect)', location: 'Throughout Nilgiri Hills, especially Kotagiri, Ooty' } ]; function TribalHeritage() { const navigate = useNavigate(); const [selectedTribe, setSelectedTribe] = useState(null); const handleBack = () => { if (selectedTribe) { setSelectedTribe(null); } else { navigate('/'); } }; return (
